title: CS1-W: constant-width linear-merge collimation with a free-frequency phase decoder

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single CS1-W algorithm and configuration of proof.md (CS1 with Kuperberg's constant-width collimation schedule: on the main branch n >= 64 every tree uses the global width W = max(1, floor(isqrt(529 n)/32) - ceil(ell/2) - ell2 - 1), where ell = ceil(log2 n), ell2 = ceil(log2 ell) and isqrt is the integer square root, so W = (23/32) sqrt(n) - (1/2) log2 n - log2 log2 n + O(1); linear-merge collimation tree, free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its total charged sequential work is T(N,s) = O(n^(2099/529) (log2 n)^(495/529) 2^((1553/736) sqrt(n))), hence T(N,s) = O(n^4 2^((1553/736) sqrt(n))) with the uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = n^4 2^((1553/736) sqrt n), whose exact growth index is 1/2. Here 1553/736 = 32/23 + 23/32, and the second bound follows from the first because (log2 n)^(495/529) / n^(17/529) is bounded for n >= 2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes; finitely many small n only affect these constants. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single CS1-W algorithm and configuration of proof.md (CS1 with Kuperberg's constant-width collimation schedule: on the main branch n >= 64 every tree uses the global width W = max(1, floor(isqrt(529 n)/32) - ceil(ell/2) - ell2 - 1), where ell = ceil(log2 n), ell2 = ceil(log2 ell) and isqrt is the integer square root, so W = (23/32) sqrt(n) - (1/2) log2 n - log2 log2 n + O(1); linear-merge collimation tree, free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(n^(3/2) (log2 n)^(-1) 2^((23/32) sqrt(n))) bits with envelope B_C(n) = n^(3/2) (log2 n)^(-1) 2^((23/32) sqrt n), whose exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes; finitely many small n only affect these constants. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single CS1-W algorithm and configuration of proof.md (CS1 with Kuperberg's constant-width collimation schedule: on the main branch n >= 64 every tree uses the global width W = max(1, floor(isqrt(529 n)/32) - ceil(ell/2) - ell2 - 1), where ell = ceil(log2 n), ell2 = ceil(log2 ell) and isqrt is the integer square root, so W = (23/32) sqrt(n) - (1/2) log2 n - log2 log2 n + O(1); linear-merge collimation tree, free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits with envelope B_Q(n) = n, whose exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes; finitely many small n only affect these constants. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single CS1-W algorithm and configuration of proof.md (CS1 with Kuperberg's constant-width collimation schedule: on the main branch n >= 64 every tree uses the global width W = max(1, floor(isqrt(529 n)/32) - ceil(ell/2) - ell2 - 1), where ell = ceil(log2 n), ell2 = ceil(log2 ell) and isqrt is the integer square root, so W = (23/32) sqrt(n) - (1/2) log2 n - log2 log2 n + O(1); linear-merge collimation tree, free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, the total number Q(N,s) of fresh source copies acquired, counting every discarded, rejected and failed-attempt copy, is at most N(n+10) on the finite branch n < 64 and at most the precomputed cap Qcap = O(n^(1570/529) (log2 n)^(1024/529) 2^((32/23) sqrt(n))) on the main branch n >= 64. Hence Q(N,s) = O(n^(1570/529) (log2 n)^(1024/529) 2^((32/23) sqrt(n))) with envelope B_samples(n) = n^(1570/529) (log2 n)^(1024/529) 2^((32/23) sqrt n), whose exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes; finitely many small n only affect these constants. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For the same CS1-W algorithm and configuration in proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
